AI Workout Coach
Step 01 · Framing

Most apps tell you what you did. Ours tells you when to stop.

An AI coach that watches you train with your phone camera and smartwatch. It recognizes the exercise, checks your form, and compares today's session with your own past sessions. When fatigue builds up, it tells you to stop before you get hurt.

Phone cameraBody skeleton, 18 joints, 30 fps
Galaxy Watch 7Heart rate + wrist motion
One decisionPer rep, in real time

Step 04 · How it works

From the gym floor to the alert

Phone camerafilms you

Laptopruns our 3 models
"Push your knees out."
Voice feedbackin under a second
1Capture

The phone films you; each frame becomes a skeleton of 18 joints. The watch sends heart rate and wrist motion.

2Model 1 · what & how many

Reads the skeleton and wrist motion: which exercise, and where each rep starts and ends.

3Model 2 · good or bad

Takes each rep cut out by Model 1 and judges it: good, or which mistake.

4Model 3 · when to stop

Combines rep speed, form and heart rate, and compares them with your past sessions.

Big data side: Kafka carries the live streams (≈ 300 messages/s) from the devices to the laptop; Spark processes every stored session to build each person's history.

Step 04 · Week 1 · big data

Spark puts three streams on one clock

The camera gives 30 skeletons per second, the watch 100 motion samples and about 1 heart-rate value. Spark joins them on the video frame number, one task per session. Slowed down 4×.

Camera · 30 / s Watch motion · 100 / s Heart rate · ~1 / s Synced row · one per frame
One real row of the Spark output · session w00

Watch motion is averaged onto the frame (≈3 samples each); heart rate is interpolated and masked when the nearest real value is over 5 s away. Never invented.

Runtime of the full job, 21 sessions
1 core57.7 s
2 cores40.9 s
4 cores37.1 s

Two cores help; after that the job waits on reading files, not on computing.

Step 06 · Week 1 · rep counting

Rep counting: the bug, then the fix

Lunges and curls alternate left and right. Our first counter followed the whole body and saw one left-plus-right cycle as one rep. The fix follows the right body part for each exercise. Same real set, both counters, 2× speed.

First counter0
Fixed counter0
Truth (label)0
First counter: whole-body movement
Fixed counter: the body part that moves once per rep
Step 07 · Week 1 · outside the dataset · RQ4 first look

A YouTube gym video the model has never seen

A RepCount-A video: new person, new camera, new gym. MediaPipe turns every frame into our 18 joints and the same camera-only Model 1 reads it.

Model 1 output

Decision taken from this test: in live use without the watch's wrist motion, we run the camera-only Model 1. The camera + watch model falls to 67.9 % when the watch data is missing.

Step 08 · Week 1 · our own data

The gym recorder: video and heart rate on one clock

Model 3 needs the same person over many sessions, with heart rate and effort scores. No public dataset has that, so we built the tool to record it: a web app in Chrome on the phone, no laptop at the gym and no watch code.

What the app guarantees
  • One clock (the phone's) for every video frame, heart-rate value and set mark: no sync step.
  • Heart rate during rests too: recovery between sets is a fatigue signal.
  • Labels at the source: exercise, reps, effort 1–10 and form after every set.
  • Checked on a real Chrome recording: 30.2 fps, frame clock within one frame (33 ms).
